messages.02bc2b5553e7e76f: The original eight bars with bass and melody, at ♩=50 and ♩=35, string-model synthesis; then each voice alone.
messages.15e3b24f9fb225eb: Play the eight bars with the click at ♩=50. On beats 1 and 3, pluck bass and melody together; the app checks both notes. On beats 2 and 4, pluck the melody while the bass rings.
messages.f1d9181ccc2fafe1: Bass and melody started together on beats 1 and 3.
messages.c2af4d6056c7dbb7: The bass rang for two full beats.
messages.0ad7decb08f4704e: I can play each voice alone from the staff.
messages.0af3ba5207199eaa: The thumb missed its string, or a finger is touching it. Aim the thumb first, then add the melody finger.
messages.48078affcaa414d9: The melody note on beat 2 or 4 waits for the bass. Keep counting; the bass rings by itself.
messages.425d6448992401c5: Play the melody alone, then the bass alone, then join them in bars 1–2 only.
messages.a02f65b817d79fe6: Uses scan, count and keep going to play four new four-bar lines once each at ♩=60.
messages.02bfa399ea5a53d4: Sight-reading means playing a line you have never seen, once, without stopping.
messages.d6f715a346c157be: Scan for 30 seconds: time signature, key signature, accidentals, highest and lowest note, and the hardest bar.
messages.e687c62cf9cc90ab: Count one bar in aloud before you start, and keep counting while you play.
messages.f6e02f338e3ad571: Don't stop. If you miss a note, skip it and come in on the next beat. The beat matters more than one note.
messages.475325cfc315dcae: Look one beat ahead of the note you are playing, not at your hand.
messages.b3436ff01bcfb595: Click at ♩=60 with a one-bar count-in. Each new line is played only after your try, so you can compare; it is not played before.
messages.f4680177355c6b8b: You get four new four-bar lines in first position. For each one: scan for 30 seconds, count one bar in, then play it once with the click at ♩=60 without stopping.
messages.7f464ae95132f4b6: I scanned each line before I played it.
messages.2a1f78d230c50836: I counted one bar in aloud.
messages.6c9d88e78a12f24d: I kept going after a slip instead of restarting.
messages.f2c70508a11aa8a0: You stopped to fix a note. Let it go and land the next note on its beat.
messages.9c9ce1967359f1f2: A sharp from the key signature was missed. Name every sharp aloud during the scan.
messages.00a693dcddd21500: Scan and play only the first two bars of each line at ♩=50, then all four bars at ♩=60.
messages.317e44bed09de3b9: Reads an eight-bar line, picks one bar to fix from the note results, and gets fewer "Different note" results on the second try.
messages.e0475fe9abd9f1f0: This lesson reads one eight-bar line twice. The first try shows where the "Different note" results fall.
messages.66077c0ce93e4010: Before the first try, scan the meter, notes, rests and the hardest string change.
messages.763888df7d650776: After the first try, open the note results. Pick the one bar with the most "Different note" results.
messages.43831127af10ec99: Fix only that bar: name each note with its string and fret, then play the bar slowly three times.
messages.640d500913b7b73d: Then play all eight bars again. Keep reading the page; don't play from memory.
messages.108a7f0819dfd7aa: The original eight-bar line at ♩=60 and ♩=40, string-model synthesis; the chosen bar can be looped alone.
messages.975573ddc00bc6a0: Play the eight bars once with the click at a tempo you choose between ♩=50 and ♩=60. Pick one bar from the note results and fix it. Then play all eight bars again at the same tempo.
messages.81bda9980237a506: Two tries at the same tempo. Passes when the second try has fewer "Different note" results than the first, or when both tries have none.
messages.a0ca6a99bb551277: I picked one bar from the results, not the whole line.
messages.466bb9fe559bf8cd: I named the notes of that bar before I played it again.
messages.804a43e223499b21: On the second try I read the page, not my memory.
messages.8c59e9a050a9bcdb: Different note, again in the bar you fixed.
messages.fd06344cb824109e: Slow that bar down further and say each note with its string and fret before you play it.
messages.44f40eab57791fe2: Use only bars 1–4 for both tries, and add bars 5–8 in a later session.
messages.1715cb00ba4f094d: Sight-reads a new eight-bar line in first position once at ♩=66.
messages.1b3b61d8bad26c92: This checkpoint gives you a new eight-bar line in first position. It is not played before your try.
messages.b2e6a2b4896608b0: The line can be in C, G or D major or A minor, in 4/4 or 3/4. It can use quarters, eighths, half and dotted notes, rests and accidentals.
messages.54ad7f010bd2613a: Use the strategy: scan for 30 seconds, count one bar in, and play once without stopping.
messages.26b52dd41032a486: Every try uses a new line. Practise at a slower tempo with new lines if you need to; the checkpoint passes at ♩=66.
messages.fca8d00c082074c1: This checkpoint completes the reading module.
messages.3613c9fe988599f3: Click at ♩=66 with a one-bar count-in. The new line is played only after your try.
messages.e1e890b1f46b4049: Scan the new line for 30 seconds, then play all eight bars once with the click at ♩=66 without stopping.
messages.2fafee3326c3264d: If it did not pass, read new lines in the sight-reading strategy lesson at ♩=60, then retake at ♩=66.
messages.45455af7222bf55f: Sets the phone distance and the flesh or nail tone so that no more than 10% of open-string notes come back as 'Couldn't hear'.
messages.f9e0f8d30d31b045: Plucked notes are quieter than strummed chords. Before this track, place the phone so the app hears every single note.
messages.590fbf9d54e924ff: Put the phone 30–50 cm away, pointing at the spot where the neck meets the body. Right in front of the soundhole, the low strings boom and cover the others.
messages.8b25e5051bff1b33: Flesh tone: pluck with the pad of the fingertip. The sound is warm and round, with a soft attack.
messages.e8b39e97f1a09c80: Nail tone: the pad touches the string first, then the string slides off a short, smooth nail. The sound is brighter and the attack clearer. If you have no nails, flesh tone is fine.
messages.59adda98fb31822d: The thumb (p) plays strings 6–4, the fingers i, m and a play strings 3–1. Keep the plucking hand still near the back edge of the soundhole; only the fingers move.
messages.2acea9e47474bb5f: The six open strings plucked one by one, first in flesh tone, then in nail tone, string-model synthesis.
messages.2c218ef76433a0a9: Tune first. Pluck the six open strings from E2 to E4 one by one in flesh tone and let each ring. Then do the same in nail tone. If more than one of the 12 notes shows 'Couldn't hear', move the phone and try again.
messages.67ed1c507b4324ba: 'Couldn't hear' on at most 10% of the notes (1 of 12), with Level 4 note accuracy.
messages.c1510f5246f97384: The phone points at the spot where the neck meets the body.
messages.4c6057c274e2d8c9: I can hear the difference between flesh tone and nail tone, as in the reference.
messages.d7034f4f41b9ce0d: Bring the phone closer, about 30 cm, and pluck a little firmer. Turn off fans or music in the room.
messages.696c51e493044a37: The fingers brush the string instead of plucking it. Press the string slightly toward the top of the guitar before you release it.
messages.c682d0d4e3ae0fbb: Use flesh tone and the thumb on all six strings until the setup passes; add nail tone in a later session.
messages.a1a49334792dc274: Keeps an alternating thumb bass on C in steady quarter notes at ♩=60.
messages.aec98b4f09a22e13: Travis picking is a fingerstyle pattern named after the guitarist Merle Travis. The thumb keeps a steady bass while the fingers add notes above it.
messages.ea84f92199b6eab5: The thumb alternates between two strings, one note per beat. On C: string 5 (C3, fret 3) on beats 1 and 3, string 4 (E3, fret 2) on beats 2 and 4.
messages.227cae30fa4953e7: Hold the full C shape (x32010), even though only two strings sound now. The fingers will need it in the next lesson.
messages.9316be3727fa1e00: Pluck downward with the side of the thumb. Move the whole thumb from its base, near the wrist; do not bend the tip joint. Rest i, m and a lightly on strings 3–1.
messages.f108a0b610780655: The bass must not wait or rush. Count '1 2 3 4' aloud with the click until the thumb runs on its own.
messages.ad96680944b4c18b: The alternating bass C3–E3 in quarter notes on C, at ♩=60 and ♩=40, with click.
messages.f59bcdd2bc8e687d: Hold C. With the click at ♩=60, play the thumb alone for four bars: C3 on beats 1 and 3, E3 on beats 2 and 4.
messages.501c3ca8aa223016: My thumb played string 5 on beats 1 and 3 and string 4 on beats 2 and 4.
messages.b18bc76dabae4583: Different note: E3 heard on a beat that needs C3.
messages.903418eede94c542: The thumb landed one string too high. Rest it on string 5 just before beat 1 of each bar.
messages.635bdc58c5a81760: The thumb rushes on beats 2 and 4. Let each bass note ring until the next click.
messages.0b01f5c0affe3671: At ♩=50, play only string 5 on beats 1 and 3, then add string 4 on beats 2 and 4.
messages.3db510694c373eaf: Adds i and m above the alternating thumb bass on C and plays the full pattern at ♩=60.
messages.cd2729ff3c5262f7: The thumb keeps the bass on the beats: C3, E3, C3, E3. The fingers fill the 'and' between them.
messages.17d070ffdd086041: Finger i plays string 2 (C4) on the 'and' of 1 and 3. Finger m plays string 1 (E4) on the 'and' of 2 and 4.
messages.d3fc13bcd30048e5: Together: p i p m p i p m, eight even eighth notes per bar. Say it aloud once before you play.
messages.c306925ce7dab926: Build it in steps: one bar of thumb alone, one bar of thumb with i, then the full pattern.
messages.3429811958e4d05a: The thumb leads. If a finger slips, keep the bass going and let the finger join again on the next 'and'.
messages.343799b3ae3cd302: The full p-i-p-m pattern on C in eighth notes, at ♩=60 and ♩=40, with click.
messages.82ba900077bcbcdb: Hold C. With the click at ♩=50, play p i p m twice per bar for four bars. When it is steady, move up to ♩=60 in steps of 5.
messages.3060c2439cbbda4b: The thumb notes fell on the clicks and the finger notes between them.
messages.7783d3bf2289e417: All eight notes in each bar sounded even.
messages.7a91214e5b0d2aa6: The thumb waits for the fingers. Play one bar of bass alone until the thumb leads again.
messages.b6c2c5891c9463b2: Different note: C4 heard where E4 is expected.
messages.078d44effa34725d: i and m swapped strings. Rest i on string 2 and m on string 1 before you start.
messages.c8a370831778d219: The finger notes are too soft next to the bass. Pluck i and m a little firmer than the thumb.
messages.58739cd727b2e56a: Use only p and i (C3 C4 E3 C4) until the bass stays steady, then add m.
messages.29f672c9a274dc44: Travis on G, Am, D and E
messages.b433174b611ec661: Moves the Travis pattern to G, Am, D and E, two bars each, at ♩=60.
messages.9105de1fcf042e44: The pattern stays p i p m. Only the strings under the thumb change, following the root of the chord. The fingers always stay on strings 2 and 1.
messages.ea3797c9b14e99ed: G (320003): root on string 6. The thumb plays G2 and D3 (strings 6 and 4); the fingers play B3 and G4.
messages.c90601eaa62c2393: Am (x02210): root on string 5, like C. The thumb plays A2 and E3; the fingers play C4 and E4.
messages.da6f1aa2009c4991: D (xx0232): root on string 4. The thumb moves over to strings 4 and 3: D3 and A3. The fingers play D4 and F♯4.
messages.500dd61a12e95ea5: E (022100): root on string 6, like G. The thumb plays E2 and E3; the fingers play B3 and E4. Before each new chord, find the root string with the thumb first.
messages.806563397a9d6cb5: The p-i-p-m pattern on G, Am, D and E, two bars each, at ♩=60 and ♩=40, with click.
messages.3b090f3993d51996: With the click at ♩=60, play the pattern for two bars each on G, Am, D and E. Move the thumb to the new root string during the last eighth of the bar.
messages.d4c2d79527b23d8e: The thumb found the root string of each chord on beat 1.
messages.25bfc1565678d4d4: The fingers stayed on strings 2 and 1 for all four chords.
messages.afb3d27e019522c7: Different note: string 5 heard on beat 1 of G or E.
messages.3b3220b6be0b5280: In G and E the root is on string 6. Move the thumb to string 6 before beat 1.
messages.36ebd30ab5f9b8e0: Different note in D: string 5 or 6 heard.
messages.5327dfe6361d0571: D starts on string 4. Move the thumb to strings 4 and 3 for the two D bars.
messages.df33525fa6415f13: On each new chord, play one bar of thumb alone first, then the full pattern.
messages.0e9dcce39a27ce59: Keeps the Travis pattern going through C–Am–F–G, two bars each, at ♩=70.
messages.8a88060a25ee12c4: The pattern must not stop at a chord change. Use the last eighth of the bar to move; the thumb lands on the new root on beat 1.
messages.c497a84ec5cd58a8: C to Am: the finger notes stay the same, C4 and E4. Keep fingers 1 and 2 down and move only finger 3 from string 5 to string 3. The bass becomes A2–E3.
messages.cb03384c786ff072: F: the full barre (133211). The thumb plays F2 and F3, the fingers C4 and F4.
messages.f871b37bda9061d3: G (320003): thumb on G2 and D3, fingers on B3 and G4. Then back to C.
messages.a0815627e9db82f4: Practise each change alone: the last two eighths of one chord and the first two of the next, in a loop.
messages.a57c74fc7f1e3dbc: The eight bars C–Am–F–G in the p-i-p-m pattern with a soft bass-and-percussion loop, at ♩=70 and ♩=45. Headphones recommended.
messages.72356f521055ee5e: Play the eight bars at ♩=60 with the loop: two bars each of C, Am, F and G. Keep the thumb going through every change. When it holds, move up to ♩=70 in steps of 5.
messages.17a1267e9a63470c: The thumb never stopped at a chord change.
messages.01702ca23313ffd8: The bass stopped at the change. Keep the thumb going, even if the new chord is not complete on beat 1.
messages.0b6acde2473dbbc5: Different note on F: F3 not heard.
messages.25f3a761bb9baa76: Finger 4 is not pressing string 4 at fret 3. Press it closer to the fret, or use the four-string F.
messages.6b82b66d80639040: Use F on four strings (xx3211) with the thumb on F3 and A3, and play each chord for four bars.
messages.e2c1b9f9d3039077: Adds a pinch on beat 1 of the Travis pattern for four bars at ♩=60.
messages.d8a1ea25fd6c793c: A pinch is the thumb and a finger plucking at the same moment. In Travis picking it marks the start of the bar.
messages.da848b37d5a17d7d: On beat 1, play p and m together: the bass and string 1 sound as one. On C that is C3 with E4; on G it is G2 with G4.
messages.99a394aa9c0e7d7f: The rest of the bar stays the same: i, p, m, p, i, p, m.
messages.55e65d1fffffcc81: Move thumb and finger toward each other, like a small pinch, then release. Both notes should be equally loud.
messages.a3bdaf2a3b85531f: Keep the pinch exactly on the click. It is the anchor; the eighths that follow hang from it.
messages.cd3116a773c3323d: The four bars C–C–G–C with a pinch on each beat 1, at ♩=60 and ♩=40, with click.
messages.7355b6b6fe72e3f9: With the click at ♩=60, play two bars of C, one bar of G and one bar of C. Start each bar with a pinch, then continue the p-i-p-m pattern. A slash in the line marks two notes plucked together.
messages.7c004c291a62049b: Both notes of the pinch started at the same moment.
messages.17fa6e0403ea57c5: The pinch fell exactly on beat 1.
messages.b20511dc7712bc09: Different chord: only the bass heard on beat 1.
messages.cb84f1023d7e3223: m plucked too softly or too late. Place p and m on their strings first, then pinch.
messages.a208158ad4cb6e9b: The pinch rushes beat 1. Count '1' aloud and pinch exactly on it.
messages.5b3d06a77a33a84d: Play only the pinch on beat 1 and let it ring for the bar until p and m land together; then add the pattern.
messages.b62635e86535e37f: Plays four original fingerstyle figures with hammer-ons and pull-offs over a thumb bass at ♩=60.
messages.402d842e63183d4e: Legato joins two notes with one pluck. The plucking hand starts the first note; the fretting hand makes the second.
messages.67eaa955238a27d5: Hammer-on: pluck the lower note, then bring a finger down fast and firm right behind the higher fret. The string keeps sounding.
messages.b74cf8f8213faa9c: Pull-off: put both fingers down, pluck the higher note, then pull the top finger slightly sideways off the string, like a small pluck.
messages.961e14cfe77bf4f4: Both notes count. The hammered or pulled note should be almost as loud as the plucked one.
messages.6017508c193e761d: The thumb keeps the bass on beats 1 and 3 while the fretting hand plays the legato. In figure 3, use finger 4 for D4, because finger 3 holds C3.
messages.38c97cf23a203c2d: The four figures, each twice, in eighth notes at ♩=60 and ♩=40, string-model synthesis with soft legato attacks.
messages.6262c971a6e145e3: Play each one-bar figure twice in eighth notes with the click at ♩=60, then all four in a row. 1 Am: hammer G3 to A3 on string 3. 2 Am: pull C4 to B3 on string 2. 3 C: hammer C4 to D4, then pull back. 4 Em: hammer B3 to D4, then pull back. In the line, h marks a hammer-on and p a pull-off.
messages.7c6c64744ff0f2b1: The second note of each legato pair sounded without a new pluck.
messages.3582b65fee2d598c: The thumb kept beats 1 and 3 during the legato.
messages.0df3abf77e07d065: The hammer is too soft or too far from the fret. Bring the finger down from higher, right behind the fret.
messages.8f06310faddda726: Different note, a semitone low, after the pull-off in figure 3.
messages.6e0363ce553701b5: Open B3 sounded instead of C4. Keep finger 1 on string 2, fret 1 while finger 4 pulls off.
messages.5900d8c10a85883f: The legato note drags. Count the eighths aloud; the hammered note falls on the beat.
messages.d5d99922b9e5258d: Play each figure without the bass first; add the thumb when the legato notes sound even.
messages.b036a35b522498eb: Joins two notes with a slide in four figures and lands on each target note.
messages.9400a469484e8adc: A slide connects two notes on one string with one pluck. The finger keeps pressing while it travels.
messages.cdcd570b6929e94b: Pluck the start note, then glide to the target fret. Keep the same pressure all the way; if it drops, the note dies.
messages.c8eba1a4c3ad8b27: Stop just behind the target fret. The app checks the start note and the target note.
messages.a55aa568ec390ac9: Slides go up or down. A downward slide needs the same pressure; do not lift on the way.
messages.90fbbdd616487e54: Look at the target fret before you move, not at your finger.
messages.24f287e9327b273e: The four slides, each twice, slowly, string-model synthesis with a continuous glide between the two notes.
messages.0606a824622aae12: Play each figure twice in your own time. 1 string 3, frets 2→4 (A3 to B3). 2 string 2, frets 3→5 (D4 to E4). 3 string 2, frets 5→3 (E4 to D4). 4 open E2 with the thumb, then string 4, frets 2→5 (E3 to G3). A spaced slash marks a slide.
messages.60794ae3c09ab169: The string kept sounding all the way to the target.
messages.633e5a404175e9da: I stopped right behind the target fret.
messages.61f77ec401934c73: Pressure dropped during the slide. Keep pressing until the target note rings.
messages.bdd25cfb5a946dc2: The upward slide stopped one fret short. Look at the target fret before you move.
messages.9845ac09c31e9106: The downward slide stopped one fret early, or the upward one went too far. Slow the last part of the move.
messages.055fcbefc2f66431: Start with the two-fret slides on string 2 only; add the three-fret slide on string 4 last.
messages.5a03ec00c37e3b92: Plays the natural harmonics at frets 12, 7 and 5 on all six strings, 18 in all.
messages.f1c2ea422e21e19b: A natural harmonic is a clear, bell-like tone. You touch the string lightly; you do not press it to the fret.
messages.2288492ad1104fcd: Place the fingertip directly above the fret wire, not behind it. Pluck firmly near the bridge, then lift the finger.
messages.932f2a61f3b797de: Fret 12 sounds one octave above the open string: E3 on string 6, E5 on string 1.
messages.9abfbbef4dca2f0e: Fret 7 sounds an octave and a fifth above: B3 on string 6. Fret 5 sounds two octaves above: E4 on string 6.
messages.8586af171603cbea: Fret 7 needs the most exact spot. If the harmonic buzzes or dies, move the finger a little until it rings.
messages.f3b9ac211aaad7ef: The 18 harmonics in order, fret 12, then 7, then 5, strings 6 to 1, synthesized harmonic tones, slowly.
messages.b923cdb59815f0b9: Play the harmonics at fret 12 on strings 6 to 1, then at fret 7, then at fret 5. Let each one ring for about a second. Take your time.
messages.255f268a5a8bbcbc: My finger touched the string right above the fret wire without pressing.
messages.c5136769708548bb: Each harmonic rang for about a second.
messages.2df0d6b6307f8b5e: Different note: the fretted pitch sounded.
messages.f840e39772d85163: You pressed the string down. Only touch it, right above the fret wire.
messages.4946070c4d71c84c: Lift the touching finger right after the pluck, and pluck closer to the bridge.
messages.eeb446aac8bfccc6: Start with fret 12 on all six strings; add fret 5, then fret 7.
messages.0904d67cbe5cd719: Plays the same note with free stroke and rest stroke and makes the rest stroke fuller and louder.
messages.cbab77f7e87973eb: Free stroke: the finger plucks the string and passes above the next string. Other strings keep ringing, so you use it for arpeggios.
messages.e66257550b5a0308: Rest stroke: the finger plucks through the string and comes to rest on the next thicker string.
messages.d8cc00815d13a8be: The rest stroke pushes the string toward the top of the guitar. The tone is fuller and louder; use it for melody notes.
messages.c2f3052d9bfbcdb2: Alternate i and m in both strokes. Keep the hand still; only the fingers move.
messages.849d90506367870b: The app compares the level of the two groups in dB. You judge the tone with the self-check and the reference.
messages.dde210c5454de0e8: E4 and C4, four notes each in free stroke and then in rest stroke, string-model synthesis, so the two tones can be compared.
messages.bb770a258dee3153: On string 1, play E4 four times with free stroke, then four times with rest stroke, alternating i and m. Do the same on string 2 with C4. Then go through the self-check.
messages.73c1a11dce669763: The rest-stroke notes are on average at least 3 dB louder than the free-stroke notes, and the self-check is complete.
messages.24f482d53bacb6c3: In rest stroke my finger stopped on the next thicker string.
messages.dbb1a9af5e42bf8f: In free stroke my finger passed above the next string without touching it.
messages.40aa5d2632adad7e: The rest-stroke notes sounded fuller than the free-stroke notes, as in the reference.
messages.55afd10ac5ba046c: My hand stayed still and only the fingers moved.
messages.712aab595059f1bf: The rest stroke is too shallow. Push the string slightly toward the top before it leaves the finger.
messages.4a79812356e3282b: Use only finger i on string 1 until the two strokes sound clearly different.
messages.3ce60fe5818df5a9: Plays four arpeggio patterns selected from Giuliani's Op. 1 on C and G7 at ♩=72, including triplets and a pinch.
messages.cba78f61455cd0c8: Mauro Giuliani (1781–1829) kept the chords of his Op. 1 right-hand studies to C and G7, so all your attention goes to the plucking hand. You met four simple patterns in Level 3; these four are longer.
messages.e7f55c4f07244f64: C is x32010 with p on C3; G7 is 320001 with p on G2. Fingers: i on string 3, m on string 2, a on string 1.
messages.71c24a91919a4068: Pattern 1: p-i-m-a-m-i in triplet eighths, three notes per beat. Pattern 2: p-i-a-m in eighths; a skips over m.
messages.e5e73b875e167314: Pattern 3: p-i-m-i-a-i-m-i, one wave of eight eighths per bar. Pattern 4: a pinch of p and m, then i-a-i, twice per bar.
messages.4a84a38a09abc550: Each pattern runs over C | G7 | G7 | C. Change to G7 during the last note of the C bar; the thumb always lands on beat 1.
messages.e0ec8e715846bab7: The four patterns on C–G7–G7–C, Ostinato setting, string-model synthesis, with a click at ♩=72 and ♩=45.
messages.b5a356d2e662fd77: Play the 16 bars with the click at ♩=60: each pattern for four bars of C, G7, G7, C. Pattern 1 is in triplets, patterns 2–4 in eighths. A slash marks two notes plucked together. When it holds, move up to ♩=72 in steps of 5.
messages.13394c32b868b758: The triplets in pattern 1 stayed even, three notes per click.
messages.4a78d1f2f2002106: The thumb waits for the change to G7. Move the fretting hand during the last note of the C bar so G2 lands on beat 1.

messages.08d8956e720b4366: Amp, headphones and the mic test
messages.aaecdb89e6c540dc: Sets up an electric guitar so the phone hears all six open strings, with 'Couldn't hear' on at most 1 of 12 plucks.
messages.b201fa5abd9a737f: The app listens through the phone microphone, not through a cable. It hears the strings themselves, so an electric guitar works without an amp.
messages.7c039da85d7aaaf8: An unplugged electric guitar is quiet. Put the phone 15–20 cm from the strings, between the neck and the bridge, in a quiet room.
messages.9f85e470d90085c7: If you use a small amp, choose a clean sound at low volume. Distortion and effects blur the notes for the microphone.
messages.7bf311c709aec167: A headphone amp is for your own ears. The phone does not hear your headphones; it still listens to the strings. Keep the headphone volume low.
messages.f014b4d1ce162bb3: This test opens measured feedback for the whole electric track. If you change guitar, room or setup later, run it again.
messages.09ab71abc2fea89f: The six open strings E2 A2 D3 G3 B3 E4, up and back down, slowly, string-model synthesis.
messages.ad30f9115e78322c: Tune first. Place the phone, then pluck the six open strings from string 6 to string 1 and back, 12 plucks in your own time. Let each string ring for about one second.
messages.cdee42349bdf8f8a: At most 1 of the 12 plucks is 'Couldn't hear', and every heard string is Correct. If not, the app suggests moving the phone closer or using a small amp at low volume, then you retake the test.
messages.b25a9923745c0e7d: An unplugged electric guitar is quiet. Put the phone 15–20 cm from the strings and pick a little firmer.
messages.749049f6e57fa6b0: A fretting finger is resting on a string. Take the fretting hand off the neck for this test.
messages.624c533e5f143437: Couldn't hear: only on strings 5 and 6.
messages.d76d50140ee88223: Low strings fade fast on a solid body. Move the phone a little toward the neck pickup and pick those strings closer to the neck.
messages.29c1ebf32d21a5e1: If the test still does not pass, play through a small amp on a clean sound at low volume and retake it.
messages.935dc0da8d4f554d: Plays an eight-bar single-note line in A minor pentatonic at ♩=70 while both hands keep the unused strings silent.
messages.3ae246ab87765e48: On an electric guitar, a string you do not play can still ring. The microphone hears it as an extra pitch and may report a Different note.
messages.d5f2172082b9641b: Picking hand: rest the side of your palm lightly on the strings below the one you play, the thicker ones. Move the palm along as you cross strings.
messages.101053842f9ce9f2: Fretting hand: let the underside of the fretting finger touch the thinner strings just enough to stop them.
messages.75d05dc94c105d96: When you skip a string, the skipped string is the one that rings most. Check it first.
messages.a27242a043078bd2: Muting is light contact, not pressure. If the played note goes dull, lift the palm a little.
messages.bb7b94579e3c3c22: The eight-bar line in quarter notes, cleanly muted, with click at ♩=70 and ♩=50, string-model synthesis.
messages.f103d7a2ff22b492: Play the eight bars in quarter notes with the click at ♩=70, in the 5th-fret box of A minor pentatonic. The app counts Different note results caused by ringing strings. Then tick the checklist.
messages.49c3b8a0e5cda9e6: Level 4 note and timing accuracy. The app also shows how many Different note results came from strings left ringing; aim for fewer on each try.
messages.e5a482cd6f5a4f9c: After each note, the string I left stopped ringing.
messages.476797f6112a166c: On string skips, the skipped string stayed silent.
messages.e452edeef7862142: My picking-hand palm moved with me across the strings.
messages.643e55800b12fc18: Different note: a lower string is still ringing.
messages.238d1636ccf4b76e: Let the picking-hand palm follow you down onto the thicker strings as you move to higher strings.
messages.8324092e2f2e1b6b: Different note: a higher string is still ringing.
messages.1122c5e624a12f37: Flatten the fretting finger a little so its underside touches the thinner strings.
messages.7e19d1d0dc4cdf82: The palm is pressing on the string you play. Move it back toward the bridge and touch more lightly.

messages.3593f3c83fb76325: Hammer-on (h): pick C4 at string 3, fret 5, then bring finger 3 down quickly on fret 7. D4 sounds without a new pick stroke.
messages.64cab6083a61d8ea: Pull-off (p): hold both frets 5 and 7, pick D4, then pull finger 3 slightly down and off the string, as if plucking it. C4 sounds.

messages.60d5606539dcf6bd: Stop exactly on the target fret. Look at the target fret before you move, not at the finger.
messages.155bb7c289ee33a4: A slide is also a way to change position. Sliding D4 to E4 on string 3 (frets 7→9) moves your hand from the 5th-fret box into the 7th-fret box.
messages.eaec72969e727cb2: In the task, '/' marks a slide, up or down. The note after it is the target.

messages.4e0e8f0bd23a95c5: Pressure dropped during the slide and the string died. Keep the finger pressing the same as on the first note.

messages.c25d5fd7b97b1ac5: Hear the target first. Pick the fret above, then go back one fret and bend up until the pitch matches.

messages.c213a5c753d52903: In the task, 'b' marks a bend: pick the first note, bend to the second. The app follows the pitch and shows how many cents you are from the target.
messages.98c81d1a0694b87f: For each bend: the target fret picked, then the bend from one fret below up to the target and held, string-model synthesis.

messages.479899daa87a2d07: For each bend: the target fret picked, then the bend from two frets below up to the target and held, string-model synthesis.
messages.9be55d254ffd4234: Play each bend twice, 8 bends in all, in your own time. Hold each target for about one second. 1 string 3, fret 7. 2 string 2, fret 8. 3 string 2, fret 10. 4 string 1, fret 8.

messages.a34914080295f64e: Daniel Gottlob Türk (1750–1813) was a German teacher and organist in Halle. In 1792 he published Handstücke für angehende Klavierspieler, short pieces for beginning players.
messages.efa76b53d3aab0fc: This lesson uses No. 1, 'Aller Anfang ist schwer' (Every beginning is hard), in C major, 8 bars. The right hand plays quarter and half notes from C5 to G5, thumb on C5. The left hand holds one long note under each bar.
messages.9d8d177e3ff60938: Each left-hand note starts together with a right-hand note. So the measured run is the right hand alone, exactly as the line on screen. Then add the left hand in a second run, which is not measured.
messages.f617a939bc760dbf: Practise in two-bar sections at a slow tempo, then join them. The score and fingering on screen are an Ostinato edition, made from Türk's 1797 second edition.

messages.b0f8d41ab540fe29: The eighths rush on the way down. Count "and" aloud and land the last note exactly on beat 3.

messages.61006b535aaad94b: C major then G major, one octave up and back, both hands an octave apart, an empty bar between, quarter notes with a click, at ♩=60 and at ♩=40, piano synthesis; finger numbers for both hands on screen.

Use the empty bar to move both hands to G: right hand from G4, left hand from G3. One note per beat at ♩=60. The line shows the right hand; the left hand plays the same notes an octave lower.
messages.11ae140f79bc51be: Both hands pressed each key at the same moment.
messages.6f139455de3c2087: One hand lags behind at its crossing. Loop that bar hands together at ♩=45 and watch the hand that crosses.
messages.dd1938ac7d9c372d: In G major, one hand played F instead of F♯. Both hands play F♯ together: right finger 4, left finger 2.
messages.c1ceacd7238dddae: Play only C4 to G4 and back with both hands (left hand C3 to G3) at ♩=45. Then add the rest of the octave.

messages.5274978332686cb1: Coming down, the pattern goes three notes down: C5 B4 A4, then B4 A4 G4, and so on.

messages.d18a4b04c1cf6f3b: The left hand plays the same groups an octave lower with its own scale fingering: C3 D3 E3 is 5-4-3, D3 E3 F3 is 4-3-2.

messages.d0929c6f123b271b: Play the groups of three with the right hand, up from C4 to C5 and back down. Use the empty bar to move to the left hand and play the same groups from C3. One note per beat at ♩=60; each group fills one bar.
messages.91d13a093e0f694a: Each note kept its scale finger.
messages.b3ddda29fee5ca1c: The first note of each group was a little stronger.
messages.824c214957759af6: Different note, two white keys too high.

messages.a8516e535d7022c6: Play only the right hand going up at ♩=50, and say the first note of each group aloud.

messages.5f85f2312e1ab34e: C, G, F, D major and A harmonic minor over two octaves, each right hand then left hand with an empty bar between, eighth notes with a click, at ♩=69 and at ♩=50, piano synthesis.

messages.9a43df1a157f8b68: The root-fifth-octave pattern uses three notes: the root, the fifth above it and the root an octave higher. Then it comes back to the fifth.
messages.e53c3c672120ac68: C: C3 G3 C4 G3. F: F2 C3 F3 C3. G: G2 D3 G3 D3. Fingers 5-2-1-2 in every chord.
messages.1ff1674881bd5284: The octave is wider than a five-finger position. Let the hand open from finger 5 to the thumb without locking the wrist. Release the low note as the thumb lands.
messages.9b5d5650b92d88ff: After the last note of each chord, move the whole hand to the next root. The shape stays the same.
messages.aab8276909b86746: The root-fifth-octave pattern on C, F, G and C, with a click, at ♩=70 and at ♩=45, piano synthesis.
messages.3cbdefb31020313b: Left hand alone, fingers 5-2-1-2, with the click at ♩=70: two bars of C, two bars of F, two bars of G, one bar of C, then hold C3 for four beats.
messages.d208e5648d8d5239: The low root sounded as clearly as the thumb note.

messages.ab17e5a38ff5514b: The first note after the hand move is late. Look at the next root during the last note and move the hand in one motion.
messages.cbc6e2995857c95a: Play root and fifth only (C3 G3 C3 G3, fingers 5-2) at ♩=55, then add the octave.

messages.8fd847c68cc9658c: For C: C3 G3 E3 G3 with fingers 5-1-3-1. All three keys sit under the hand; only the fingers move.
messages.fc4271156e68bdf3: Each note is an eighth, two notes per beat. Count "1 and 2 and": C3 falls on 1, E3 on 2, and the thumb's G3 on every "and".
messages.aeabc127b341ab9a: The thumb plays every other note. Keep it light, so the bottom note leads and the pattern sounds like a soft background.
messages.246c6bbe11d798de: Let a small rocking of the wrist help the fingers, from finger 5 towards the thumb and back.
messages.e3bb998356e226bc: The C Alberti pattern in eighths for four bars, ending on C3, with a click, at ♩=80 and at ♩=55, piano synthesis.
messages.3778ca3b756a3559: Left hand alone, fingers 5-1-3-1, with the click. Play three bars of the pattern in eighths, then the pattern once more and end on C3 for two beats. Start at ♩=60 and move up to ♩=80 in steps of 5.
messages.b5e23cf2e782b076: The thumb's G3 was softer than C3 and E3.
messages.c78526cb385972e7: The eighths rush as the tempo rises. Go back 5 bpm and count "1 and 2 and" aloud.
messages.6f7c73af80e68ae3: Finger 2 played instead of finger 3: F3 instead of E3. Place fingers 5, 3 and 1 on C3, E3 and G3 before you start.
messages.e3d1346288a2c33d: The thumb's G3 is too faint at speed. Keep it light but take it to the bottom of the key.

messages.e1d3d5c31a9424bd: Plays the Alberti bass in G and in F with the left hand in even eighths at ♩=70.

messages.7fc4b986fc131294: F: F2 C3 A2 C3. Finger 5 on F2, finger 3 on A2, thumb on C3.

messages.9c32b45c674fd78c: The G Alberti pattern for three bars ending on G2, then the F pattern ending on F2, in eighths, with a click, at ♩=70 and at ♩=45, piano synthesis.

messages.692136eaf7bf1eeb: The root-fifth-tenth pattern on C and F, with a click, at ♩=60 and at ♩=40, piano synthesis.

messages.b7bfac07b5f0cdeb: Each bar starts on a note of its chord, and the last note leads by step into the next bar.
messages.d98f2e596afea2ad: Bars 1–2 lie in C position: finger 5 on C3, thumb on G3. In bar 3 the hand moves one white key down: finger 5 on B2, finger 4 on C3, finger 3 on D3.

messages.19afe924b61b7152: Play the melody with only the first note of each left-hand group, then add the full pattern.

messages.b52fd0fcb3c7a6bd: An acoustic piano can have up to three pedals. The right one is the sustain pedal. The left one makes the sound softer. The middle one differs from piano to piano.
messages.c58574e0cfb4d871: Inside the piano, a damper rests on each string and stops it when you let go of the key. The sustain pedal lifts all the dampers at once.
messages.0878787cf7b81ced: So with the pedal down, a note keeps ringing after your finger leaves the key. Lift the pedal and the sound stops.
messages.517f2aafcd9bfa6d: Use your right foot. Keep the heel on the floor and press with the front of the foot, all the way down and all the way up.
messages.458af9341b0bbce3: In a score, "Ped." means pedal down and "*" means pedal up. A bracket line under the bass staff shows the same thing; a notch in the line means up and down again quickly.
messages.aec7c04b26dcbde2: On a digital piano, plug a sustain pedal into the pedal or sustain socket. If it works in reverse, switch the keyboard off, plug the pedal in, and switch on without pressing the pedal.

messages.301596fb0de91337: This minuet comes from a music book Bach gave his wife Anna Magdalena in 1725. For a long time it was called Bach's; today it is credited to Christian Petzold (1677–1733).
messages.7dc94db5554e3d2d: A minuet is a dance in 3/4. Feel one strong beat at the start of each bar.

messages.da6ead3208042e26: Bar 4 jumps down an octave, from G5 to G4. Move the whole hand, not only a finger.
messages.d34bce0fb3f7ccd6: The second half moves to D major and uses C♯. Play the eighth notes evenly and light, the quarter notes a little longer.
messages.101ae1233b265a16: Practise in two-bar sections at a slow tempo, then join them. The score on screen is the Ostinato engraving, made from a 1906 Munich edition; fingering and tempo are ours.
messages.a23b17a6d120c485: Right hand of the Minuet in G from the Ostinato edition, piano synthesis, at ♩=80 and at ♩=56.

messages.1a7859d6378f4099: A musette is a small bagpipe. The left hand copies its drone: it stays on one bass note for a while and leaps by octaves.

Then play both hands in a second run, which is not measured, with the accompaniment softer than the melody.
messages.8c37dc0baf1778e3: Practise in two-bar sections at a slow tempo, then join them. The score and fingering on screen are an Ostinato edition, made from the 1910 Augener edition.
messages.be35cc0c6b6eea90: Gurlitt, Op. 130 No. 1, bars 1–8, from the Ostinato edition, piano synthesis: the melody alone, then both hands, at ♩=76 and at ♩=52.
messages.e7096371e51cee1d: Run 1, measured: play the melody alone, bars 1–8, with the click: first in two-bar sections, then all 8 bars at ♩=76 (one click per quarter, so each eighth note is half a click). In bar 8 play only E5 of the E5–B4 pair. Run 2, not measured: play both hands as written.
messages.24b41c15bdffd381: The melody was louder than the accompaniment.
messages.ef2a235184b302ef: Each phrase had a high point and a soft ending.
messages.f511a54ec41efd76: Plays a study from Czerny's Op. 599 evenly at ♩=80.
messages.44c0a2dbf424800a: Carl Czerny (1791–1857) was a pupil of Beethoven and a famous teacher. His Op. 599 is a set of short studies for beginners.
messages.c12656a4df4d7e5a: This lesson uses No. 12, one of the five-finger exercises 'with a quiet hand'. The right hand runs in eighth notes between C5 and G5 without moving the hand. The left hand holds one three-note chord in each bar.
messages.7b4d49ef1c1883c0: Evenness is the goal: every note at the same time distance and the same loudness.
messages.b50fac6619a2177b: Start slowly. Raise the tempo in small steps only when the slower one passes.
messages.4e580ad1b9ec35ba: Each left-hand chord starts together with a right-hand note. So the measured run is the right hand alone, exactly as the line on screen; add the chords in a second run, which is not measured. The score and fingering on screen are an Ostinato edition, made from the Holle edition of about 1850.
messages.64be02e832b61a17: Czerny, Op. 599 No. 12, from the Ostinato edition, piano synthesis: the right hand alone, then with the chords, at ♩=80 and at ♩=56.
messages.b48cc8f6fb43e559: Run 1, measured: play the right hand alone, bars 1–16 without the repeats, eighth notes two per beat. Practise in two-bar sections at ♩=56, then play all 16 bars at ♩=80. Run 2, not measured: add the left hand, one held chord per bar.
messages.b94a97d2aeed856b: The running notes were even in time and loudness.
messages.8cd299061a3a1710: A thumb crossing or a hand shift is late. Loop those four notes at ♩=56, then rejoin the study.
messages.a4015bf52885465a: Soft fast notes are hard to separate. Play each note a little deeper into the key.
messages.396df0b01af2ebfa: Play the study at ♩=66 until it passes, then go up in steps of 5 to ♩=80.
messages.d7824019bf44cc3d: Plays a later study from Beyer's Op. 101 at ♩=80.
messages.79161f3d6c70bfdb: Ferdinand Beyer (1803–1863) wrote Vorschule im Klavierspiel, Op. 101, a step-by-step beginner book. You played an early study from it in Level 2.
messages.d5f884799722d68b: This study is No. 61, Allegro moderato, in G major, 16 bars. The right hand sings a dotted tune high up, between G5 and G6. The left hand plays a broken-chord accompaniment in quarter notes, G3 D4 B3 D4, with C4 in some bars.
messages.980aabcd6de31b0b: The left hand plays on every beat. On beats 1 and 3 it usually starts together with the right hand: there the line on screen shows the right-hand note, and the left-hand note is not measured. The left-hand notes that start on their own, mostly D4 on beats 2 and 4, are measured.
messages.0f1cce84a4656dc9: Practise in two-bar sections at a slow tempo, then join them. The score and fingering on screen are an Ostinato edition, made from the 1895 Peters edition.
messages.548698c5b32a5892: Beyer, Op. 101 No. 61, from the Ostinato edition, piano synthesis, at ♩=80 and at ♩=56.
messages.e377c8141ce138ea: Play each hand alone once with the click. Then join the hands in two-bar sections, and play the study from start to finish, bars 1–16, at ♩=80. Both hands play every note; on beats where they start together, only the right-hand note is measured.
messages.84e96c1c3f5ad5d3: Every hand shift was ready before the note.
messages.acdcfc6da994067e: Plays Melodie, Op. 68 No. 1, by Robert Schumann with a singing melody over a quiet accompaniment.
messages.451558cf68acacf6: Robert Schumann (1810–1856) wrote Album for the Young, Op. 68, in 1848 for his daughters. Melodie is the first piece.
messages.7140ba21daa8169b: The right hand sings the melody. The left hand plays a calm line below it, and the hands often start notes together.
messages.a75f74702ed140de: It is in C major and 4/4, 20 bars long. The left hand plays eighth notes almost all the way; the right hand mostly plays quarter notes, with a few two-note chords.
messages.756a4ccc90b71b4e: Play legato and let the melody sound above the left hand.
messages.2c88505bc64c4061: There is no target tempo. Choose a calm tempo at which every note is clear.
messages.bdb91c3a4ccbe848: Melodie, Op. 68 No. 1, from the Ostinato edition: melody alone, then both hands, calm and legato, piano synthesis.
messages.43b799627f93aa52: Play the right hand alone once, then the left hand. Then play the piece with both hands at a calm, steady tempo, without the repeat of bars 1–4.
messages.b87120d8f42c3a4a: The notes were connected, with no gaps.
messages.2289bc0d3c838c32: The hands drift apart. Play the two bars around the slip slowly and press both keys at the same moment.
messages.7c8f19c08aa9cf61: Play the melody with only the first left-hand note of each bar.
messages.4c925ef6a3a9b12f: Minuet in G minor (Notebook for Anna Magdalena)
messages.d223121a285f769b: Plays the right hand of the Minuet in G minor, BWV Anh. 115, from start to finish at ♩=80, then tries it with both hands.
messages.d52d4d6b72427f56: This minuet comes from the music book Anna Magdalena Bach started in 1725. In the book it comes right after the Minuet in G. Like that minuet, it was long called Bach's; today it is credited to Christian Petzold (1677–1733).
messages.bce923eaaaa1d4d5: It is in G minor and 3/4, with two halves of 16 bars. The key signature has B♭ and E♭. Watch the extra signs: E♮ in bars 17 and 29, F♯ in bars 27, 29 and 31.
messages.5229497b5a40b6e6: The right hand is measured. The left hand plays a slow bass line, mostly half and quarter notes with a few two-note chords. Add it in a second run; that run is not measured.
messages.943791ab915918ef: Bar 31 has a quick figure: B♭4 as an eighth, then C5 and D5 as two sixteenths. Play it light and land on G4 on beat 2.
messages.159a3863a6ec2112: The Minuet in G minor from the Ostinato edition: right hand alone, then both hands, piano synthesis, at ♩=80 and at ♩=56.
messages.e0e8bce3c55b9f7d: Run 1, measured: play the right hand alone with the click, first in two-bar sections, then bars 1–32 at ♩=80, without the repeats. Run 2, not measured: play the minuet with both hands from the score.
messages.6d9f144d560f1d85: Plays the first four bars of Hanon No. 1, each hand separately, in even eighth notes at ♩=60 without tension.
messages.2c22f8e5060884bf: Charles-Louis Hanon (1819–1900) published Le Pianiste virtuose in 1873. Exercise 1 repeats one pattern, one step higher each bar.
messages.c11a555a3456a13e: The pattern from C: C E F G A G F E. Right hand 1-2-3-4-5-4-3-2. Left hand, an octave lower, 5-4-3-2-1-2-3-4.
messages.e7bc9321c0b040e2: The hand spans a sixth, wider than a five-finger position. Open the hand gently between fingers 1 and 2; do not force it.
messages.95968795a2234c22: Hanon writes these notes in sixteenths. Here you play them in eighths at ♩=60, a careful first tempo.
messages.629a655d8d148d12: Fast repetition builds tension quickly. Keep the wrist loose, and stop and shake the hand out if the forearm tightens.
messages.c177fc9ea557ab48: Hanon No. 1, bars 1 to 4, right hand from C4, then left hand from C3, eighth notes with a click, at ♩=60 and at ♩=45, piano synthesis.
messages.c2812d719fd8d24e: Right hand from C4: play bars 1 to 4 in eighth notes at ♩=60, two notes per beat. Rest one bar. Left hand from C3: the same four bars.
messages.8336142b882690a0: Every note was as loud as its neighbours, fingers 4 and 5 too.
messages.3a29df61584c674d: My hand opened for the sixth without strain.
messages.b8a4c3a4d5d74e76: Finger 4 or 5 is too light. Let the arm weight lean slightly toward the little finger.
messages.a7dab17da40b71d6: The jump back to the next start note is late. Move the hand on the last eighth of each bar.
messages.18fbdaf8e0a500a8: Play bars 1 and 2 only, in quarter notes at ♩=60, then go back to eighths.

messages.6280a6be9abe7052: Start slowly enough to play with no slips. A slow clean try teaches more than a fast messy one.
messages.e5849bdcca47d7dd: Loop the hard spots. Play two bars around the slip three times clean, then join them to the bars before and after.
messages.5063f564764c2f1b: Climb the tempo ladder: from ♩=60 up in steps of 5. Go to the next step only when the current one passes.
messages.ceac84d15fb9bb18: Finish with a run-through: play the eight bars once without stopping, as if someone were listening.
